en.title: A job interview
en.summary: Typical interview questions and how to answer them honestly and clearly.

paragraphs: An interview is a conversation with a purpose: the employer wants to know who you are, and you want to show what you can do. This lesson prepares you for the questions you are most likely to hear.
Sam is at an interview for a job as a shop assistant in Bristol.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Thank you for coming, Sam. Tell me a little about yourself.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I am twenty-three. I worked in a cafe for two years, and I enjoy helping customers.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Why do you want this job?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I like your products, and I'd like to learn more about retail.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I'm reliable and I work well in a team. I'm also quick to learn new things.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I could start next Monday, if that suits you.

paragraphs: **1. The past simple tells your experience.** Use it with a finished time such as for two years or last year. Regular verbs end in -ed; many common verbs are irregular. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
PresentPastExample
workworkedI worked in a cafe.
managemanagedI managed a small team.
teachtaughtI taught children.
leadledI led a project.

paragraphs: **2. I'd like to and I'd love to state wishes politely.** They are short forms of I would like to and I would love to. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FormExample
I'd like to + verbI'd like to learn more.
I'd love to + verbI'd love to join your team.
I could + verbI could start on Monday.
I'm interested in + -ingI'm interested in working with people.

items: Strengths are things you do well; a weakness is something you want to improve.
Reliable means that people can depend on you; punctual means on time.
Arrive ten minutes early, dress smartly and shake hands.
Prepare one or two questions to ask at the end.

paragraphs: Interviewers in Britain and the United States like short, honest answers supported by an example from your own experience. Boasting is not admired, and neither is false modesty.
